draft.title: Patrons and the Medici
card: A patron is a person or family who pays artists and scholars to produce work. In Renaissance Italy, many artists relied on patrons for money and commissions.
The Medici were a rich banking family in Florence. They used their wealth to pay for paintings, sculptures, buildings and scholars' work.
Patrons gained more than art. Grand works showed off their wealth and power, and they helped build the patron's name and standing in the city.
Artists such as Michelangelo had support from the Medici at times. Patronage meant artists could spend their time on their work, but patrons often had a say in what was made.
draft.remember: Patrons paid for art, and in return the art displayed their wealth and power.

a.q: Why did a wealthy patron such as the Medici pay for grand public artworks?
opts: To show off their wealth and power
To lower the cost of art for the poor
To stop artists from studying ancient texts
To let artists choose their own subjects
a.why: Grand works showed the patron's wealth and power and built their standing in the city. Patrons often had a say in what was made, so paying for art did not mean artists chose freely.
a.clue: Think about what the patron gained from the art.

b.q: In Florence, a banker pays a sculptor to make a huge statue for the town square, and has his family crest carved on it. What does this show?
opts: Patrons used art to display their wealth and power
Artists in Florence could not find any paid work
Bankers wanted to hide their wealth from the city
Sculptors were only paid when they worked for the Church
b.why: Paying for a large statue with a family crest on it displays the family's wealth and power to everyone in the square. The crest shows the banker wanted to be seen, not hidden.
b.clue: Why put a family crest where everyone can see it?

a.best: To show off their wealth and power

b.best: Patrons used art to display their wealth and power
